_why: The status check contexts branch protection requires on `main`, declared in-tree so a
rename can be caught by the auditor instead of by an unmergeable `main`. brik-llm#1914
established the shape; brik-llm#2519 extended the auditor to reach this repo.
A context in `contexts` MUST be the job name of a workflow triggering on
`pull_request` or `pull_request_target` with NO `paths:` filter, no `types:` narrower
than [opened, synchronize, reopened], and no `branches:` filter excluding `main`. A
restricted trigger that does not match produces no check-run at all — not a skipped
one — so protection waits forever on a status that never reports (brik-llm#1937 arm B).
`require-area-label` is the job in pr-label-gate.yml, a `pull_request_target` workflow.
That trigger reads its workflow FILE from the base branch, which is why the gate could
not police its own introducing PR (#1988) — but it reports normally from the next PR
onward, and #1993 verified both directions live on #1998: label removed produced a
check `failure` and `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`; label re-added produced `success` and
`CLEAN`.
`visual` (#2077) satisfies the no-`paths:` rule but not the way the others do. It
cannot be workflow-level filtered — that is the brik-llm#1937 arm B failure — so the
diff test moved INSIDE the workflow: a `classify diff` job emits an empty shard matrix
on an inert diff, and the aggregate job named `visual` runs `if: always()` and reports
green (visual.yml:320-350). Job-level, not trigger-level, is the only shape that gets
both a skip and a required context. Do not 'tidy' it into a `paths:` list.
`naming-canon-check` and `canonical-class-check` (#2086) are plain unfiltered gates —
they were promotable as-is precisely because #2069/#2070 never filtered them. The
seven added in #2038's second wave are the same shape: `base-freshness`,
`cascade-contract-check`, `closing-keyword-guard`, `esm-bundle-check`, `gitleaks`,
`require-issue-link`, `rsc-smoke`.
`reconcile` (merge-reconcile.yml) is NOT here and must never be. It triggers on
`pull_request: types: [closed]`, so it cannot report on an OPEN pull request — the
types rule above, not the paths rule. Requiring it would block every merge on a
context that only exists after the merge. It is the post-merge detector whose
standing `needs:reconcile` queue `require-issue-link` exists to prevent.
`tokens-gate` (#2098 slice 1) is the visual.yml shape applied deliberately rather than
out of necessity, and it is the template for four more groups. Seven token gates —
color-ramps, contrast-gate, token-purpose-slot, token-self-reference, token-shadow,
tokens-studio, widget-tokens — were each trigger-filtered and therefore each
permanently ineligible. They now run as STEPS of one `token lints` job behind a
`classify diff (tokens)` job, with the aggregate `tokens-gate` job reporting
`if: always()`. Two rules govern any edit to it:
1. The classifier's pathspec is the UNION of the seven former `paths:` lists. Never
narrow it to the group's theme — a job-level filter that sees less than the
trigger did turns a required check into one that passes because it never ran.
`token-purpose-slot-check`'s broad `components/**` is preserved for exactly this
reason, not by accident.
2. Every lint step runs `if: always()` so one red does not hide the other six, gated
on `steps.install.outcome` so a failed `npm ci` does not fake thirteen failures.
`docs-gate` (#2098 slice 2) folds nine documentation gates in — bcs-vocab,
token-cascade-vocab, mdx-coverage, mdx-deprecation, mdx-heading, mdx-token,
component-props, doc-links, docs-site-build — and it is the variant to copy when a
group is NOT cost-uniform. It has THREE work jobs, not one, because two members are
expensive and their old triggers were narrower than the group: `doc links` needs
`build-storybook` (13s) and `docs-site build` needs `build:lib` plus a second cold
`npm ci` against docs-site's own lockfile (16s+). One shared job would have made a
`tokens/**`-only change pay both, since mdx-token-check watches `tokens/**` while
docs-site-build.yml's trigger was `docs-site/**` ALONE. So the classifier emits one
boolean PER WORK JOB, each the exact union of only THAT job's members' former paths.
That satisfies rule 1 more tightly than a group-wide union does, and it keeps the two
heavy members running in parallel instead of serially. A third rule comes from it:
3. Job ids in a group gate must be HYPHEN-FREE (`doclinks`, not `doc-links`).
`needs.doc-links.result` parses as SUBTRACTION in an Actions expression, so the
aggregate's assertion silently never matches and the gate passes on a failing
job. Display `name:` keeps the hyphen; only the id changes.
`contracts-gate` (#2098 slice 3) folds twelve script-contract gates in and is the
cost-uniform case again, so ONE work job like tokens-gate. Its lesson is about shared
SETUP, not just a shared runner: NINE of the twelve each ran `apt-get update &&
apt-get install shellcheck` in their own runner — nine apt-get updates for one
binary. Grouping collapses that to one step, and it is most of why the whole group
now runs in ~50s. Two rules came out of it:
4. Install a shared tool ONCE in the work job, and keep every member's invocation
of it VERBATIM as its own step. The shellcheck thresholds differ per file on
purpose (`-S warning` for libs carrying pre-existing info-level SC2016, plain
default for the sweeper); flattening them into one call quietly raises or lowers
a bar the plumbing PR has no mandate to touch.
5. Do NOT drop an install just because the runner image already has the tool.
ubuntu-latest ships shellcheck, and session-budget-contract.yml relied on that
and was green — but the nine that installed it were tuned against the NEWER apt
build, so dropping the install silently changes which findings they see.
`standards-rag-drift-check` is inside contracts-gate and is safe there: its `--check`
mode only verifies pairing on disk and does NOT need the brik-rag CLI
(run-standards-ingest.sh:61-63), which is why a required context does not become
dependent on a machine-local tool. It is also the one member needing git history, so
the work job checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`.
`storybook-recipe-check` and `storybook-story-shape-check` were promoted in #2142 by
dropping their `paths:` filters — the individual-gate route, not a group gate. That
PR did only one of the change's three halves: it POSTed the contexts but did not
declare them here and did not fix their concurrency, so for ten days this auditor
reported [protection-drift] every morning (morning-check.sh:2151-2152) AND could not
see that both were cancelling. Rules 6a/6b only evaluate contexts that are DECLARED,
so the drift HID the wedge. #2322 fixed both halves; the lesson generalises:
6. A promotion is THREE changes, not one — drop the filter (or move it to job
level), declare the context here, and make the concurrency non-cancelling. Doing
the POST alone leaves a required context that can wedge `main` green, and the
missing declaration is what stops the auditor telling you.
`assets-gate` (#2098 slice 4, #2328) folds four registry gates in — contact-icons,
service-icons, social-icons, logo-registry — and is the cost-uniform case, so ONE
work job like tokens-gate. Every member is the identical shape: checkout, `npm ci`,
one dependency-free `gen:<set>:check`. The install is essentially the entire cost, so
four runners collapse to one. Its union pathspec is worth one note, because the
obvious tidy-up is a rule-1 violation both ways: `components/ui/*/icons/**/*.svg`
reads like the group's theme but silently drops `assets/logo-*.svg`, and widening to
`components/**` would make every component PR in the org's Actions hot spot pay the
gate. All twelve entries stay listed exactly as the four triggers listed them.
`assets/logo-*.svg` is a glob that may legitimately match nothing — an allowed state
the pathspec linter permits by design (lint-gate-pathspecs.mjs:36-38).
Its promotion (#2328 AC7) took FOUR changes, not rule 6's three, because #2416 landed
ten hours after #2363: the merge_group migration below enumerated the 17 contexts
DECLARED at the time, and `assets-gate` was not one of them, so it was excluded by
construction. Declaring it without `on: merge_group` would have dropped
`lint-merge-queue-readiness.mjs --enforce` to 17/18 and silently blocked the ruleset
flip. The generalisation: a group gate built BEFORE its promotion PR inherits every
requirement added to the required set in between — re-run the readiness auditor, do
not count the changes from rule 6 alone.
The remaining 11 PR workflows carry a trigger-scoped `paths:` filter and are
therefore ineligible until they move the diff test to job level, the way visual.yml,
tokens-gate.yml, docs-gate.yml, contracts-gate.yml and assets-gate.yml did.
`brik-llm/scripts/audit/pr-trigger-scan.py --root . --repo brikdesigns/brik-bds`
prints the split. TEN of them are #2098's one remaining group (components, #2329) —
not the eleven #2098's decision comment lists, because #2142 promoted
storybook-recipe-check and storybook-story-shape-check individually and
blueprints-astro-check is newer than that comment, so re-read the scan output rather
than the comment before starting it.
The ELEVENTH is `md-creation-gate.yml`, which landed in #2353 after #2098's groups
were drawn and belongs to neither. A filtered gate added after the grouping is not a
defect — it is the default shape — but it means the scan's filtered count and
#2098's group membership are no longer the same number, and closing #2329 will NOT
take the count to zero. Route it deliberately rather than folding it into the
components group by arithmetic.
The components group carries a trap worth naming before anyone starts it: `test.yml`
filters with `paths-ignore`, NOT `paths`. It skips on `**/*.md`, i.e. exactly the
docs-only PR the promotion AC tests with, and its `cancel-in-progress: true` fails
rules 6a/6b. It needs its own conversion, not the group shim.
`merge_group` readiness (brik-bds#2415): every context above ALSO triggers on
`merge_group` now. GitHub couples merge-queue required checks to the
branch-protection required checks here — a gate that fires only on
`pull_request` never reports on the merge group, so the queue wedges the same
way brik-llm#1937 arm B wedges a PR. The trivial and diff-logic gates run their
real work on the rebased merge-group head (base..head via
`github.event.merge_group.base_sha`/`head_sha`); the three metadata gates
(`require-area-label`, `require-issue-link`, `closing-keyword-guard`) report
green on `merge_group` because the queued PR already passed them. Two contexts
are fleet-canonical twins: `gitleaks` carries an in-place brik-bds divergence
(like its #2038 concurrency block, from the canonical security template), and
`closing-keyword-guard`'s `merge_group` trigger + short-circuit is a DECLARED
brik-bds delta in brik-llm `overlap-twin-drift.py` GUARD_DELTAS. Readiness is
asserted by `node scripts/lint-merge-queue-readiness.mjs --enforce` (18/18 since
`assets-gate` joined the set in #2328 AC7).
The queue is LIVE on `main` as of 2026-09-11, and `--enforce` is GATED (#2447):
contracts-gate.yml's `merge-queue readiness` job runs it on any PR touching
`.github/required-checks.json`, `.github/workflows/**`, or the linter itself. It
is a separate job with its own classifier arm, NOT a step in `script contracts`
— the contracts' pathspec list does not name either input, so a promotion PR
(the only shape that can break readiness) skips it. HOW the queue is configured
is UNVERIFIED: repo rulesets are empty (`gh api repos/brikdesigns/brik-bds/rulesets`
→ 0) and branch protection carries no merge-queue key; the org ruleset needs
`admin:org`, which this token lacks. That it is live is not in doubt —
`mergeQueue(branch:"main")` returned live entries and two PRs merged through
`gh-readonly-queue/main/*` on 2026-09-11.
ORDERING RULE, established by the #2444 incident: land the `merge_group` trigger
on `main` BEFORE the declare + POST, never the same moment or after. GitHub reads
the trigger from the MERGE-GROUP ref, not from `main`, so a promotion POSTed first
self-satisfies its own group (which carries the PR's own commit) while wedging
every group built on the older `main`. #2444's group `pr-2444-1bf02fff` reported
`assets-gate` green; #2446's `pr-2446-38f36e02`, built on the pre-merge `main`,
produced NO check-run at all, sat AWAITING_CHECKS at position 1, and blocked
#2444 behind it. Repair took a `dequeuePullRequest` on #2446, letting #2444 land
the trigger, and a re-enqueue. This is rule 6's three changes plus a sequencing
constraint: the trigger PR merges, THEN the declaration + protection POST.
Editing this file does NOT change protection. Apply it with:
brik-llm/scripts/audit/required-check-contract.py --root <this repo> --check-protection
to see the drift, then PATCH .../branches/main/protection/required_status_checks.
Use that sub-endpoint, never the full-object PUT on .../protection — the PUT drops
every setting you omit.
Gate: brik-llm/scripts/audit/required-check-contract.py
Gate's test: brik-llm/scripts/audit/tests/test_required_check_contract.py
